title: The Pawn Chain
subtitle: The Base, The Head, and the Direction of Attack
summary: The structural backbone of the chessboard: identifying the head and the base of the pawn chain, the cardinal rule of attacking the base, and navigating the two theatres of war.
aphorism: A pawn chain is a fortress whose strength lies in its links. Never attack the head where it is strongest; lay siege to the base, and the entire structure will collapse.
attribution: 100th Anniversary Centenary Edition. Newly authored prose and interactive studies inspired by Aron Nimzowitsch (1925).

body.historicalContext: Nimzowitsch's theory of the pawn chain transformed how chess players evaluate closed positions (such as the French Defence and King's Indian). He provided a geometric roadmap for where and how to attack.

sections.title: Anatomy: The Head and the Base
sections.markdown:
A **[[pawn-chain|pawn chain]]** is a diagonal formation of connected pawns protecting each other.

- **The Head**: The most advanced pawn (here, **e5** for White, **d5** for Black). The head points toward the flank where you hold space and should conduct your attack.
- **The Base**: The rearmost pawn that is *not* defended by another pawn (here, **d4** or **c2** for White, **c6** for Black).

moves.comment: White asks Black's bishop for its intentions.
Black exchanges the bishop for the knight.
White recaptures, strengthening the c3-d4 chain.

sections.title: The Golden Rule: Attack the Base!
sections.markdown:
Why do we attack the **base** rather than the head?

If you attack the head (**e5**), you strike at the pawn that is already supported by the entire chain behind it. But if you undermine the base (**d4** with **...c5**), the foundational support is severed, and the advanced pawns become defenseless orphans.

moves.comment: Black closes the queenside and locks White's bishop out.
White retreats the bishop to maintain kingside attacking lines.

sections.title: The Two Theatres of War
sections.markdown:
The direction of the pawn chain dictates the **two theatres of war**:

- White's chain points toward the **kingside** (d4-e5), so White's natural attacking theater is the kingside.
- Black's chain points toward the **queenside**, so Black must seek counterplay on the c- and b-files.

engineLens.takeaway: Stockfish confirms that respecting the direction of your pawn chain yields high coordination, whereas attacking on the wrong wing leads to severe positional disadvantage.

drills.title: Siege the Base
drills.markdown: White has erected a pawn chain on d4-e5. As Black, strike at the base of White's chain with your c-pawn.

hints.text: Push your pawn from c7 to c5 to attack d4.

feedback.correct: Right on the mark! 1...c5 directly assaults White's d4 foundation.
feedback.wrong: Play ...c5 to challenge the base of White's pawn chain.
